candidates.tagline: Apple's $2,000 foldable cracks at the fold after fewer than 20 opens
candidates.story: Apple's iPhone Duo, launched October 23 at $1,999, began showing inner-display cracks along the hinge crease within days of purchase — with some users reporting failure after fewer than 20 folds — and iFixit's teardown identified a hinge support bar that appears to press into the OLED panel; Apple acknowledged 'an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units' and offered free replacements.
candidates.why_funny: The iPhone Duo's entire design premise is that folding is a feature — and the flaw is that it cannot fold without breaking.
candidates.alt: Close-up of an iPhone Duo's inner OLED display showing a T-shaped crack running horizontally from the fold crease toward the screen edge, the damaged area showing dead pixels and display separation

candidates.tagline: Ballon d'Or website named Kane the winner — and Mbappé — and Yamal — all at once
candidates.story: Hours before the October 26 Ballon d'Or ceremony at London Palladium, the award's official website accidentally published pre-written 'winner' articles for multiple nominees simultaneously — declaring Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappé, and Lamine Yamal each the 2026 winner — because France Football had prepared a full article for every nominee in advance and their CMS published all of them; Kane ultimately won for real.
candidates.why_funny: The organization whose entire brand is a year-long dramatic build-up to a secret reveal had their website spoil it — for three different winners at once — because they prepared all the endings but forgot to lock the drafts.
candidates.alt: Harry Kane in a white England shirt, mid-stride on the pitch during England vs Ghana on 23 June 2026, the same player the Ballon d'Or website prematurely named winner of the award alongside two other nominees
